newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Strong sterling takes experts by surprise.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Strong sterling takes experts by surprise.

text.p: Sterling's rampant rise in recent months against the dollar and the mark has caught experts by surprise, according to a review of the forecasts made last year in a Reuters survey of predictions for the British economy.
Predictions for the pound against the dollar made in a survey exactly a year ago showed that $1.4951 was the mean of 35 forecasts for December 31, 1996.
The highest prediction for cable at the close of the year was $1.63.

But the actual rate at the end of the year was $1.7120 following a dramatic rise which traders say is the result of strong fundamentals and Britain's relative isolation from the storm of currency convergence ahead of European currency union.

The experts were also caught out by the rise of the pound against the mark. This time last year, a total of 35 experts were polled and their average prediction was 2.2257 marks for the close of business on December 31, 1996. The actual rate was 2.6380.

The analysts were more successful in their predictions for British interest rates, which are currently at 6.0 percent after a 25-basis-point rise last October. Eleven out of 40 forecasters got it right.
Traders still see more gains for sterling against the mark despite a near-20 percent rally from 2.2220 marks at the start of 1996 to a 52-month high of 2.6767 last week.
Some traders are betting on a rise above 2.80 into territory not seen since the pound left the European exchange rate mechanism in September 1992.

But for the record, the latest Reuters survey of 31 forecasts puts sterling-mark at a more modest 2.4509 by the end of this year, and the pound, according to an average of 35 predictions, will be trading at 1.6154 dollars when 1998 dawns.
